variants.note: The style's own proportional_system states the parti in these words: no elevation reads as symmetrical and the front door is not at the centre of the facade.
The style's own massing_affinities calls the symmetrical double-pile block 'the failure mode of the style, not an expression of it.'
bay_rhythm is additive, not rhythmic; an even, repeating bay spacing has, in the style's own words, 'left the style.'

composition_parti.note: eclectic-revivals leaves symmetry class to each member to state; this is Tudor Revival's own.

variants.note: defining_characteristics: 'one or more prominent front-facing cross-gables of unequal size' -- the plural, unequal cross-gable is as central to the type as the single gable inherited from the family.

roof_form.note: The family's front-gable binding (germanic-vernacular) is retained as the base gable-fronted case; this adds the style's own signature plural, unequal cross-gable massing.

pitch_typical.note: Midpoint of the style's own stated 10:12-16:12 range.

cross_gable_relative_to_main.value: must equal or exceed the main roof pitch, never shallower

roof_pitch.rule: Main roof pitch not less than 10:12, typically 10:12 to 16:12; a subordinate cross-gable's pitch must equal or exceed the main roof, never shallower. Below 10:12 the style's own hard constraint (c03) voids it.
roof_pitch.note: Specified rather than extends: the inherited family default (british-picturesque, minimum 45 degrees = 12:12) is a STRICTER floor than this style's own sourced 10:12 (~39.8 degrees) minimum, so merging would silently tighten the style's own documented range instead of expressing it. This style's own numbers, sourced from its own constraint c03 and proportional_system, replace the family default outright.

variants.note: The style's identifying gable treatment; distinguished_from names its absence as the single test that returns a building to Colonial Revival, and its formalisation into stone with no timber at all as the test that moves it to jacobethan-revival.
The parapeted, shaped gable belongs to jacobethan-revival, the formal masonry wing of the same import; its presence here is exactly the tell distinguished_from names for that variant.
A flush gable with no timbering or bargeboard has, per the style's own diagnostic_tells, 'left the style' the same way a level ridge or a resolved timber corner would.

gable_treatment.rule: The gable end is half-timbered -- stuccoed infill within applied timber members that must describe a structurally plausible frame (c01, c02) -- never parapeted, never left flush.

plan_width_min.note: Hard constraint c05: not less than 3'0" wide in plan.

projection_from_wall_min.note: c05: projects at least 12 in from the wall face; a flush or concealed flue is, in the style's own words, incoherent.

chimney.note: The family's tall-multiple-vertical-accent variant (british-picturesque) already states the chimney is deliberately oversized and a primary vertical accent; this adds the style's own specific plan dimensions from its hard constraint c05.

variants.note: The style's own long description names this as the decisive economic fact: 'the perfection of masonry veneer... gave American builders the appearance of English mass at American labour rates,' and it is the reason the style could descend from estates to $6,000 suburban houses within twenty-five years.
Where the half-timbered upper storey is genuinely structural rather than a veneered pattern, on the more architect-designed examples.
The grander estate examples -- Meadow Brook Hall's 'genuinely varied stonework.'

construction_type.rule: Masonry-veneer-over-frame is the type case, not the fallback: the style's whole diffusion from millionaire estate to speculative suburb runs on veneer over a wood frame at American labour rates.
construction_type.note: Specified rather than extends: the inherited value (english-classical, solid-masonry-two-wythe canonical, masonry-veneer-over-frame FORBIDDEN as fatal) is not a partial mismatch to refine but the opposite ranking for this style's single most economically significant construction fact.

variants.note: The lower storey, per the style's own defining_characteristics: 'masonry or stone below.'
The upper storey; stuccoed infill within applied timber -- see gable_treatment and secondary_cladding.
The all-brick single-material Georgian wall this slot would otherwise inherit (english-georgian) is exactly what this style's multi-material rule (c04) contradicts.

primary_cladding.rule: The wall is multi-material by design, not by accident: masonry or stone at the ground storey, stuccoed half-timbering above, changing at a floor line or jetty (see material_change_rule).

variants.note: Stuccoed half-timbering above the masonry storey -- the style's defining two-material wall, directly overriding the family's single-material rule.

secondary_cladding.rule: A second material above the ground storey is not merely permitted but required: the style's own defining_characteristics name the horizontal material change between storeys as one of six necessary features.
secondary_cladding.note: Overrides the family's inherited single-cladding-material prohibition (georgian-colonial-american), which is correct for the classical wing of this family and wrong for Tudor Revival's whole formal argument.

min_offset_in.note: Hard constraint c04: a minimum 4 in horizontal offset, or a water table, at the change.

material_change_rule.rule_append: The change must occur at a floor line or at a projecting jetty; a material change stopping mid-storey without the offset is forbidden (c04).
material_change_rule.note: The inherited Arts-and-Crafts material-honesty rule (british-arts-and-crafts) already states the principle correctly; this adds the style's own sourced number for where and how much.

window_proportion.note: The family's overall grid ratio (tudor-jacobean) states the whole window's width:height; this adds the style's own sourced individual-casement-leaf dimensions from its typical_ratios.

cluster_size.note: Casements grouped in 2, 3, or 4, per the style's own typical_ratios.

window_grouping_rule.rule_append: Clusters do not align between storeys; any facade producing an even, repeating bay spacing has left the style.
window_grouping_rule.note: The inherited horizontal-band rule (british-arts-and-crafts) is refined with the style's own specific cluster count and its own explicit non-alignment rule.

variants.note: No classical order is used anywhere in this style (order, column, pilaster, entablature are family-forbidden below); the inherited pilasters-and-entablature answer belongs to the family's classical wing, not this one.

form.value: a Tudor (four-centred) arch, or a heavy round-arched masonry surround, usually recessed and set within a projecting gabled bay

door_surround.rule: The entrance is framed by a four-centred Tudor arch or a heavy round-arched masonry surround, never a classical order.

variants.note: The garage as a lower, subordinate cross-gable wing continuing the wall's own material change and roof pitch -- one more picturesque volume in an already additive massing, rather than an applied box.
A garage door on the principal elevation substitutes a flat, rhythmic opening for the deliberately non-resolving asymmetrical composition the whole style depends on.

door_orientation.value: turned off the principal elevation wherever the lot allows
door_orientation.note: OQ 18, 24 Aug 2026: reclassified from `editorial` to `invented`. The two are different claims -- the schema defines editorial as 'our considered convention' and invented as 'no precedent exists' -- and `garage_strategy`'s own ontology note says in its first sentence that no historical precedent exists. A number about the garage door itself cannot be a convention drawn from tradition, because the tradition has no garage. The parameters left editorial on this slot are the ones carried from the dependency tradition rather than invented for the garage: subordination, ridge ratio, pitch match, cladding continuity.

roof_pitch_match.note: The garage wing's roof continues the main roof's own pitch and material, never a shallower applied lean-to.

garage_strategy.rule: No traditional precedent exists; the garage is authored as one more subordinate gabled volume in the style's own additive massing vocabulary, its door turned away from the approach.

variants.note: The entrance is 'recessed and often placed in a projecting gabled bay' rather than fronted by a freestanding porch.
The compressed suburban version, where the picturesque is reduced to one gable and one chimney.
A freestanding classical portico is the family's classical answer, and this style forbids the order it would require.
A full-width porch reads as a single continuous datum, which fights the picturesque asymmetry the style's own bay_rhythm and massing depend on.

porch_type.rule: The threshold is compression before release: a low, recessed, shadowed entrance under its own gabled bay, not a freestanding classical portico.
